title: Grey-box prototype vs bot
problem: We do not know yet whether three real-time lanes can be followed on a portrait phone screen, or whether giving hero orders on top of playing cards is fun. No released game has proven either. A cheap prototype played against a computer opponent answers both before any server, store or art spending.
scope: A web game that opens from a link on a phone, in portrait
Map: 3 lanes, 1 tower per lane per side plus a Core, two jungle strips with one camp each, long winding middle lane, early tower shield
One resource (placeholder name "mana"): start 5, max 10, +1 every 2.8 s, double speed in the last minute
One fixed deck of 8 cards (6 regular + 2 heroes), 4 in hand, next card shown; cards snap onto a lane
Minion waves every 20 s in every lane
Two heroes (Ranger, Warden): stay on the map, level 1-4, respawn, abilities fire automatically
Five hero orders by dragging the portrait: push, defend, gank (through the jungle, hidden), farm, retreat
Win by destroying the Core; at time-out more towers wins; then 1 minute of sudden death; then a draw
Game rules in their own module, whole-number maths only, no graphics code inside
Result screen with a rematch button

acceptance.text: A full match can be played from a link on a phone in portrait, from start to result screen
acceptance.evidence: Automated part passed: scripts/phone-check.cjs at iPhone 13 size played controls and a full match to the result screen ('PHONE CHECK OK'); also checked at Pixel 7 size inside the preview frame. Waiting for the owner to play on their own phone.

acceptance.text: Same starting seed and same moves give exactly the same match result (rules are deterministic)
acceptance.evidence: npm run verify: tests/determinism.test.ts 4/4 pass (same seed run twice identical at every step; logged moves replay exactly in 3- and 2-lane modes; human-style moves vs bot replay exactly)

acceptance.text: Each of the five hero orders (push, defend, gank, farm, retreat) makes the hero do the right thing
acceptance.evidence: npm run verify: tests/orders.test.ts 7/7 pass (push, defend, gank hidden + Ambush, gank same lane = push, farm +2 mana then old order, retreat heals at Core, order kept through respawn); browser check: dragging a portrait onto a camp gave Farm

acceptance.text: Bot against bot: 100 matches finish with no errors
acceptance.evidence: npm run soak: 'SOAK 100 matches in 42.6 s, results {blue:22, red:22, draw:56, core:14, towers:30, sudden:0}, average match 322 s'; plus 20 two-lane matches; all finished, no errors

acceptance.text: The 2-lane / 3-lane switch works (2 lanes = the two side lanes)
acceptance.evidence: tests/lanes.test.ts 4/4 pass (3 lanes = 3 towers a side; 2 lanes = side lanes only, waves only there, full match finishes); phone-check: '?lanes=2 starts a match with only the side lanes'

acceptance.text: Owner plays 5 or more matches on their own phone and notes: readable? fun? which lane count?

risks: Grey shapes may undersell the fun
The browser may run slowly on a cheap Android phone; check early
Hero orders on top of cards may still be too much to track; T6 is there to catch it
All numbers are first guesses and will need tuning
cost: RM0. Free tools; preview is a private web link. About 1-2 build sessions (estimate).
userNotes: First playable prototype: one-on-one against a computer opponent on a three-lane portrait map with a long, winding middle lane.
Two hero cards (Ranger, Warden) that stay all match, level up and take orders: push, defend, gank, farm, retreat.
Settings: 2 or 3 lanes, game speed, easy or normal bot.
